findings.summary: pyeq compiles `x and y` / `x or y` in a value position to 0/1, not to the operand Python returns: wrong proved=True, and proved=False with overflow_only=True
pyeq drops every bare expression statement that is not a call: walrus, yield and raising expressions vanish, giving wrong proved=True
pyeq ignores decorators: a function wrapped with functools.wraps is compiled undecorated
pyeq accepts range() and range(stop=3) as empty loops, and a shadowed range as the builtin, proving equal functions that raise TypeError on every input
Model.solve reuses its solver when a new constraint adds no variable: the model returned violates the constraint, and a contradiction reads as SAT
Model.solve after Model.solutions keeps the blocking clauses: None on a satisfiable model
A Python bool in an expression becomes literal 0 or 1 of variable 0: m.add(True), b | False and a == b on BoolVars all constrain the first variable
at_most_k and exactly_k with k < 0 are satisfiable; the sum cannot be negative
IntVar.ge and le assume a sorted domain: wrong solutions on int_var([2, 1])
A repeated domain value gets two literals and is_ knows one: x != 1 still allows 1
at_most_one([]) and exactly_one([]) with method='totalizer' die with RecursionError
pyeq reports a width the circuit does not have: an unused key in widths claims 'equivalent at 8 bits' for a 4-bit circuit, and no parameters claims 0 bits for 8
pyeq ignores positional-only parameters, then crashes with TypeError building python_outputs for a counterexample
proof_steps differs between the engines, as tests/test_pyeq.py documents; a field disagreement that is not a bug
Model.solutions() without project repeats user-level solutions, one per state of the auxiliary variables, under a docstring that says distinct
differential_solve compares a CNF with itself when a model uses only all_different, sum_leq, sum_geq or parity
pyeq accepts widths of 0 and below and proves anything at them, and treats an unknown engine name as Python

not_checked: Model(config=...): every model runs under the default Config
Model has no engine parameter, so native is judged on the Model's CNF, not through Model.solve
Encoder gates called with an explicit out=, and Encoder features the Model API does not expose (campaign/gen_encodings.py owns them)
Optimiser.run(target=...), max_iterations and resuming; only optimise() is run
a weighted optimum has no API, so it is judged by bounding sum_leq at the optimum and one below
CNF checks by DPLL look at up to 32 user assignments per model, not all of them
unprojected solutions() is capped at 2000 models per instance
EncodingDisagreement raised by a genuinely wrong encoding: none occurred, and no stub injects one
pyeq above 9 input bits or 7 bits of width: the oracle enumerates every input
pyeq's python_error field: no generated function raises in Python
ProofRejected: no proof was rejected, and no stub injects a bad proof into pyeq
pyeq on methods, closures and callables without source, beyond the probes
